name: H. Ross Perot, Sr.
profile: Founder of Electronic Data Systems (EDS) and Perot Systems; died July 9, 2019 in Dallas.
notes: Deceased (d. 2019-07-09), source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot. Son Ross Perot Jr. runs the family business (Perot Group/Hillwood).

name: Boris Berezovsky
profile: Russian businessman (LogoVAZ, ORT, Sibneft) and political figure; died March 23, 2013 in Ascot, England.

name: Emilio Azcárraga Milmo
profile: Mexican media magnate who ran Televisa ('El Tigre'); died April 16, 1997. Son Emilio Azcárraga Jean succeeded him.

name: Reinold Geiger
current_role: Chairman and executive director, L'Occitane Group (Geneva-based)
profile: Austrian-born (Dornbirn, 1947) engineer and INSEAD MBA who began investing in Provence cosmetics maker L'Occitane in 1994 and built it into a group of brands (Elemis, Sol de Janeiro, Erborian etc.) in 100+ countries. He stepped down as CEO in 2021 and took the company private with Blackstone in 2024; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: L'Occitane was the first French company to list in Hong Kong (2010); Geiger then delisted it in 2024 with Blackstone. The group became a certified B Corp in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a carpenter, he studied engineering at ETH Zurich; before L'Occitane he founded several small firms, including a tourism company in London, and in 1978 founded AMS Packaging in Paris, which made cosmetics packaging, later sold at a profit.
notes: Lives in Geneva. In a 2012 INSEAD interview he said he expected to be a hands-off investor in L'Occitane and 'just wanted to have no boss'. Best route: group communications.

name: Xu Gaoming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and executive director, Laopu Gold Co., Ltd. (HKEX: 6181)
profile: Hunan-born (1964) founder of Laopu Gold, the 'Hermes of gold' luxury jeweler known for traditional Chinese 'heritage gold' craftsmanship, fixed pricing and a small number of palace-style stores. After a decade in government he started a souvenir/cultural-products business in 1995, launched Laopu in 2016 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2024; the stock's surge made him one of China's richest.
interesting_fact: Laopu runs only a few dozen stores, yet in H1 2025 each generated an average of ~459m yuan in sales; its Tmall flagship became the first gold jewelry brand to exceed 1bn yuan in the 618 festival.
deep_cut_fact: He started out around age 20 as a clerk at the fisheries bureau of Yueyang near Dongting Lake, and earned his degree in 1988 via a correspondence program with Huazhong Agricultural University. He has said the brand 'seeks to both preserve tradition and rebel against tradition'.
notes: No published personal/press email found; company IR contact details should be in Laopu Gold's HKEX annual report (hkexnews.hk, stock code 6181). Says he expects gold prices to keep rising; expanding abroad starting with Southeast Asia.

name: Akira Mori
current_role: Chairman, Mori Trust Co., Ltd.; founder and chairman, MA Platform
profile: Kyoto-born (1936) Tokyo property developer, son of Mori Building founder Taikichiro Mori. He and brother Minoru inherited the family business in 1993 and split it in 1999; Akira built Mori Trust (Marunouchi Trust City, Tokyo Shiodome Building, Conrad Tokyo and ~30 hotels). In 2016 he handed the CEO role to his daughter Miwako Date and became chairman.
interesting_fact: Mori Trust helped create Japan's REIT market and listed Mori Trust Sogo REIT; the group also brought Conrad and Shangri-La hotels to Japan and turned around the historic Karuizawa Manpei Hotel.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 12 years as a banker: after graduating in economics from Keio in 1960 he joined Yasuda Trust and Banking, only joining Mori Building in 1972; in 1973 he founded Mori Trust Hotels & Resorts.
notes: Input record listed only 'Akira' (shared with Minoru Mori, Forbes 1996-98); this is Akira Mori of Mori Trust. Age ~90; daughter Miwako Date runs day-to-day operations. Route via Mori Trust corporate contact.

name: Wei Shaojun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Longjitaihe Group (隆基泰和), Hebei
profile: Hebei-born (1963, Gaobeidian) founder of Longjitaihe, a privately held Baoding-area property developer that started in construction in the mid-1990s and partners with state-run Hebei Port Group. He later expanded into solar (2008) and became controlling holder of listed Tongda Power (通达动力) in 2017.
interesting_fact: Longjitaihe moved into photovoltaics in 2008 and in 2017 Wei became the actual controller of listed motor-components maker Tongda Power.
notes: Low public profile; little reliable English coverage. Not the same person as Tsinghua chip scholar Wei Shaojun (WEF profile) - avoid confusion. Biographical data from Chinese profile sites only; verify current status before outreach. Dropped off rich lists after 2022.

name: Liora Ofer
current_role: Chairperson, Ofer Investments and Melisron Ltd (TASE)
profile: Haifa-born (1953) real estate businesswoman who inherited Ofer Investments, cofounded in 1957 by her father Yuli and uncle Sammy Ofer. She has chaired Melisron since 2008, growing it into one of Israel's largest property companies (malls incl. Ramat Aviv Mall, office parks), and now owns 100% of Ofer Investments.
interesting_fact: She is one of only two female billionaires in Israel (the other being Shari Arison); under her chairmanship Melisron acquired 25 shopping malls from British Israel Investments.
deep_cut_fact: She began working alongside her father at Ofer Investments at age 20, and in 1995 became general manager of Coral Beach Eilat Ltd, the Red Sea hotel business, years before taking over Melisron.
notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is via Melisron's corporate/IR office (melisron.co.il; site was unreachable during research). Recognized as a donor to Reichman University (IDC Herzliya): https://runi.ac.il/en/about/runifriends/donor-recognition/liora-ofer

name: Karen Pritzker
current_role: Investor and philanthropist; president, The Seedlings Foundation; co-founder, LaunchCapital (seed fund); co-founder, KPJR Films
profile: Granddaughter of Hyatt/Marmon founder A.N. Pritzker and daughter of Robert Pritzker (input lists name as 'Pritsker'). Her wealth derives from the family's Hyatt and Marmon holdings. Based in Branford, Connecticut, she co-founded seed investor LaunchCapital in 2008 and executive-produces documentaries on education and child health.
interesting_fact: Through KPJR Films, co-founded with James Redford in 2012, she executive-produced Sundance-selected documentaries 'The Big Picture: Rethinking Dyslexia' (2012) and 'Resilience: The Biology of Stress and The Science of Hope' (2016).
deep_cut_fact: Before investing and philanthropy she worked as an editor at Working Mother magazine (until the family sold it in 1986) and wrote for Seventeen, Success, Kirkus Reviews and Newsday.
notes: Seedlings funds local, ad-free news (e.g. New Haven Independent, CT Mirror, American Journalism Project) - a natural hook for a journalist. Seedlings does not accept unsolicited proposals. Runs the Pritzker Vlock Family Office.

name: Li Ganpo
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jingye Group (敬业集团), Hebei/Beijing
profile: Founder of Jingye Group, a large private Chinese steelmaker (rebar, plate, sheet, rails) with interests in chemicals, pharma, logistics, tourism and 3D-printing metal powders. He started with a chemical plant in 1988, entered steel in 2002, and in 2020 bought British Steel out of insolvency; the UK government took control of British Steel in 2025.
interesting_fact: Jingye's first fortune came from chemicals (acid) before steel; the group also built roads, housing and schools and provides healthcare and higher education for employees and the local community.
deep_cut_fact: A former teacher, he founded a canning factory and a brewery in Pingshan county near Beijing in 1985, then the Jingye chemical factory in 1988; 'jingye' means 'dedication'. He served in the 11th National People's Congress from 2008.
notes: Low media profile. British Steel ownership dispute with UK government (2025-26) is sensitive - avoid as an outreach hook. No published personal/press contact found; route would be via Jingye Group corporate office.

name: Subae Mohammad Ibrahim Mohammad Ai (Mohammed Ibrahim Al-Subaei / family)
profile: Hurun entry (2023-24) appears to be a garbled rendering of Mohammed Ibrahim Al-Subaei / Mohammad Ibrahim Al Subaei & Sons Co., the largest shareholder (~19.3%) of Saudi Arabia's Bank Albilad. Sheikh Mohammed Ibrahim Al-Subaei, who co-founded the business with brother Abdullah (from a money-exchange shop serving pilgrims), died 18 Aug 2017 aged nearly 100.
notes: Namesake patriarch deceased (2017): https://amlak.net.sa/en/17098/ ; brother Abdullah died 2021: https://www.leaders-mena.com/?p=10720 . Wealth now sits with heirs via Mohammad Ibrahim Al Subaei & Sons Co. (stake per https://www.argaam.com/en/tasi/albilad/profile). Unclear which living family member Hurun meant; not researched further.

name: Ronald Burkle
current_role: Co-founder, President, Chairman and Managing Partner, The Yucaipa Companies; Executive Chairman, Soho House & Co
profile: Pomona-born (1952) investor who rose from bagging groceries at Stater Bros. to founding private-equity firm Yucaipa in 1986, rolling up supermarket chains (Fred Meyer, Ralphs, Food4Less, Dominick's). Yucaipa now invests across hospitality, sports, entertainment and logistics; he is executive chairman of Soho House and a co-owner/investor in pro sports teams.
interesting_fact: As co-owner of the Pittsburgh Penguins with Mario Lemieux he won multiple Stanley Cups; the Penguins were called the only North American team with private-equity ties to win a championship. He is also lead investor in Sacramento Republic FC.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the United Food and Commercial Workers union (Local 770) at 13, graduated high school at 16 and entered Cal Poly Pomona to study dentistry; at 29 he tried a secret leveraged buyout of Stater Bros. backed by Charlie Munger.
notes: Known for union-friendly dealmaking and Democratic fundraising. Best route: Yucaipa press relations. Avoid political/legal topics in outreach.

name: Wenchi Chen (Chen Wen-chi)
current_role: President and CEO, VIA Technologies (since 1992); HTC co-founder/director
profile: Taipei-born (1955) chip engineer, educated at National Taiwan University and Caltech, who has run x86/chipset maker VIA Technologies since 1992. With his wife Cher Wang he co-founded smartphone pioneer HTC; Forbes ranked the couple Taiwan's richest in 2011. VIA now focuses on embedded/AI edge systems while HTC centers on VR (Vive).
interesting_fact: In 2011 Forbes ranked Cher Wang and Wen-chi Chen as Taiwan's wealthiest people, at US$8.8 billion, on the back of HTC's smartphone boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before VIA he was a senior architect at Intel and VP of sales & marketing at startup ULSI, and co-founded and ran Symphony Laboratories, a chipset firm acquired by Winbond in 1995.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Cher Wang (Forbes lists jointly). Both are devout Christians and have been described as running their companies on biblical principles. Route via VIA press room.

name: Chen Zhiping
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Smoore International Holdings (HKEX: 6969), Shenzhen
profile: Hunan-born (1975) founder of Smoore, the world's largest maker of vaping hardware (FEELM atomization tech, Vaporesso brand), supplying Japan Tobacco, BAT and NJOY. He joined the Shenzhen startup as a minority shareholder in 2007, led it to a 2020 Hong Kong IPO and has diversified into medical inhalation and beauty devices.
interesting_fact: Smoore's 2020 Hong Kong IPO raised more than $900 million and made Chen China's first vaping billionaire; at the 2021 peak his fortune was reported near 99 billion yuan.
deep_cut_fact: A Tongji University marketing graduate, he began as a salesman at a Shanghai tech firm after graduating in 1997 and later was a sales manager at Fudan Guanghua Information Technology; his first entrepreneurial venture, trading coal, failed before he turned to e-cigarettes.
notes: Extremely low-profile, almost never gives interviews. Vaping is regulation-sensitive; frame outreach around manufacturing/tech (atomization, medical inhalation). Route via Smoore IR.
